subject.name: Mechanics
subject.description: Grade 11 Semester 1 Mechanics develops a conceptual and quantitative understanding of forces, vectors, work, energy, and motion. Students analyse friction, vector operations, work-energy relationships, conservation of mechanical energy, and power through problem-solving and real-world applications.

content.title: Unit 1 (Lo1)
content.description: This unit covers friction and force analysis, including kinetic friction, static friction, normal force, free-body diagrams, and the coefficient of static friction.

concepts.title: Kinetic friction
concepts.description: Kinetic friction acts against motion when two surfaces slide relative to each other.

concepts.title: Static friction
concepts.description: Static friction resists the tendency of motion before sliding begins.

concepts.title: The normal force
concepts.description: The normal force is the contact force exerted perpendicular to a surface in response to an applied load.

concepts.title: Free-body diagrams
concepts.description: Free-body diagrams isolate an object and show the forces acting on it so the system can be analysed.

concepts.title: Coefficient of static friction
concepts.description: The coefficient of static friction represents the maximum frictional force that can develop before motion begins.

content.title: Unit 2 (Lo2)
content.description: This unit introduces vector operations, including dot product, vector magnitude, angle between vectors, and cross-product of two vectors.

concepts.title: Dot Product
concepts.description: The dot product combines two vectors to produce a scalar that depends on their magnitudes and the angle between them.

concepts.title: Magnitude (length) of a vector
concepts.description: The magnitude of a vector measures its size and is calculated from the square root of the sum of squared components.

concepts.title: Angle between vectors
concepts.description: The angle between vectors describes the separation between their directions in space.

concepts.title: Cross-product of 2 vectors
concepts.description: The cross-product of two vectors produces a third vector perpendicular to the plane containing them.

content.title: Unit 3 (Lo3)
content.description: This unit focuses on the work-energy theorem and the relationship between work and change in kinetic energy.

concepts.title: Work-Energy Theorem
concepts.description: The work-energy theorem states that the net work done on an object equals the change in its kinetic energy.

content.title: Unit 4 (Lo4)
content.description: This unit investigates conservation of mechanical energy, gravitational potential energy, kinetic energy, potential energy, and spring potential energy.

concepts.title: Conservation of mechanical Energy
concepts.description: Mechanical energy is conserved when only conservative forces are doing work on the system.

concepts.title: Gravitational Potential Energy
concepts.description: Gravitational potential energy depends on an object’s height in a gravitational field.

concepts.title: Kinetic Energy
concepts.description: Kinetic energy measures the energy of motion and depends on mass and speed.

concepts.title: Potential Energy
concepts.description: Potential energy is stored energy based on an object’s position or configuration in a field or system.

concepts.title: Spring potential energy
concepts.description: Spring potential energy is stored in a stretched or compressed spring, according to Hooke’s law.

content.title: Unit 5 (Lo5)
content.description: This unit introduces power as the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred.

concepts.title: Power
concepts.description: Power is the rate of doing work or transferring energy and is measured in watts.

content.title: Revisions
content.description: This section groups revision videos covering the major Mechanics midterm content, including LO1 and LO2 review material.
